To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) recent neural video compression algorithms can be viewed as instances of a general stochastic temporal autoreg- ressive transform; (2) this transform can be enhanced by using hierarchical latent vari- able models; and (3) the proposed hierarchical autoregressive modeling for neural video compression outperforms the state-of-the-art in terms of rate-distortion performance.

(1) recent state-of-the-art video compression models can be viewed as a special instance of a generalized temporal autoregressive stochastic transform; (2) we propose a hierarchical autoregressive model that outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of rate-distortion performance on large-scale video datasets; and (3) our model is able to compress videos with higher resolution than the state-of-the-art.

(1) we show a connection between neural video compression methods and autoregressive gener- ative models; and (2) we show that this connection enables us to improve neural video compression methods by combining masked aut- oregressive flows and hierarchical latent variable models.

our work is a step towards better understanding of the connection between generative modeling and video compression, and we show that it leads to a better performing method for the latter task.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an autoregressive model that is capable of modeling video data in a way that is compatible with the task of video compression.
we propose a new neural architecture based on a hierarchical autoregressive model for video compression.
the hierarchical autoregressive model can be used to improve neural video compression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the task of lossless and lossy video compression can be viewed as a special case of sequential density estimation.
the hierarchical structure of the autoregressive model is key to its superior performance, and that this structure is well-suited to the task of neural video compression.
hierarchical autoregressive modeling is a powerful paradigm for sequential data compression.
